I.evidence: "the regional gap you're working against holds at 4,227 openings a year" — regional≠institutional held exactly; footprint and share trace to returned figures (200.3, 0.051, 101, 0.026).

II.evidence: "the demand figures are the Centers of Excellence 2024–2029 projection, and supply is a 3-year average of DataMart completions" — two provenance notes, not a wall; practitioner language throughout, no tool/field names.

III.evidence: "Want to go to the occupation level to see where the gaps concentrate?" — offers next moves, makes no value call or recommendation.

IV.evidence: "Those two programs are Electronics and Electric Technology ... supporting 8 occupations ... and Energy Systems Technology ... 5 occupations" — walks member→sector→program→occupation and teaches how grain interacts with regional vs member figures.

V.evidence: "the most recent single year can run higher or lower" — volunteers a limit and provenance unasked, keeps the gap (4,227) and Skyline supply/share consistent across all three turns with no drift.

worst_failure: On the figure-dense turns the analyst gives provenance but never explicitly offers the corroborating dashboard view, so the practitioner is never invited to verify the numbers with their own eyes at salience.
fix_points_at: The DOCTRINE clause implementing Principle V's 'offer the view to verify with their own eyes' — surface the corroborating dashboard link on figure-dense turns where doing so would not break concision.
establishment_evidence: "let me switch the frame from Skyline alone to the whole district. San Mateo County CCD is the district-level view; it spans its colleges (Skyline is one of them)" — grounds Skyline at college grain first, re-grounds to the district on the switch without a premature scoped measure, then explains the scope (district ⊇ college) doubles the footprint while the regional gap holds.
